subject.title: [Bug]: Managed Memory Dreaming Promotion cron silently NO_REPLY since 2026-05-09 (jobs.json lastRun stays null)

question: When a managed Dreaming cron run handles the trigger but one or more workspaces fail or produce no durable Dreaming output, should OpenClaw mark the cron run as failed/partial, keep cron success but surface doctor/Dreams diagnostics, or close this as fully covered by the SQLite-state fix?
rationale: Changing this behavior affects operator-visible scheduler semantics for a maintenance job and may alter how existing users interpret cron success, so it needs maintainer intent rather than an autonomous narrow fix.

options.title: Surface Partial Failure
options.body: Treat per-workspace Dreaming failures as a cron-visible failure or partial-failure outcome and add doctor/status coverage for the failed workspace count.

options.title: Doctor-Only Visibility
options.body: Keep cron run status as success for handled maintenance turns, but make doctor/Dreams status report recent failed Dreaming events and stale diary output.

options.title: Declare Fixed By SQLite
options.body: Close this as covered by the shipped SQLite-state migration and ask for a fresh issue only if current-release cron or doctor output still hides a reproduced failure.

recommendation.title: Surface Partial Failure
recommendation.body: Treat per-workspace Dreaming failures as a cron-visible failure or partial-failure outcome and add doctor/status coverage for the failed workspace count.

likelyOwner.reason: The same history shows steipete authored the SQLite-state fix and is the strongest recent owner signal for the affected memory-core state and diagnostics surfaces.
